facts.statement: Rhegminornis calobates was an extinct species of turkey that lived in Florida during the early Miocene.
facts.quote: Rhegminornis calobates is an extinct species of turkey from the early Miocene of Florida.

facts.statement: The species was described by Alexander Wetmore in 1943.
facts.quote: It was described by Alexander Wetmore in 1943.

facts.statement: Fossils of this species are known from the Early Miocene (Burdigalian) Alachua Formation at the Thomas Farm site.
facts.quote: It is known from the Early Miocene (Burdigalian)-aged Alachua Formation of the Thomas Farm site.

facts.statement: Rhegminornis calobates is classified in the class Aves, order Galliformes, family Phasianidae, and subfamily Meleagridinae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves ordo: Galliformes familia: Phasianidae subfamilia: Meleagridinae

facts.statement: Rhegminornis calobates is the only known species in the genus Rhegminornis.
The genus Rhegminornis lived between 18.5 and 16.3 million years ago during the Burdigalian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Burdigalian (18.5 to 16.3 million years ago)
